kjv: he hath set the world in their heart
mine: he has put eternity into man's heart
note: Hebrew ha'olam in biblical Hebrew means "long duration, eternity"; the sense "world" is post-biblical. Some read 'elem "ignorance". The KJV's "world" reflects later usage.

kjv: God requireth that which is past
mine: God seeks what has been driven away
note: Hebrew nirdaf is "the pursued/persecuted" (or "what has passed by"); the KJV interprets it as past time being called to account.

kjv: the spirit of man that goeth upward
mine: whether the spirit of man goes upward
note: MT vocalises ha'olah and hayyoredet with the article ("that goes up / that goes down"), as the KJV does, probably to avoid doubting the afterlife; the LXX, Vulgate and syntax favour the interrogative "whether ... whether", making it a question about human destiny. Context: a question: who knows whether (high confidence). 3:19-20 'all go to one place, all are from dust' and 3:22 'who can bring him to see what will be after him?' are sceptical.
